S4-08.name: Room status lifecycle, soft deletion, and maintenance periods
S4-08.statusBehavior: Status and room_status_history are persisted atomically. No-op transitions are rejected; DECOMMISSIONED is terminal; general room PUT cannot change status. History stores old/new status, changedByUserId, reason, and generated changedAt.
S4-08.softDeletion: Room deletion sets deleted_at. Deleted rooms are hidden from normal room reads/lists and mutations, while the room row, status history, and room-owned child rows remain stored; status history remains queryable for deleted rooms.

PostgreSQL checks cover weekdays, working-window order, nonempty closure ranges, recurrence end dates, and positive occurrence counts. PostgreSQL tstzrange is mapped by a Scheduling-local Hibernate UserType.

S5-02.name: Calendar and working-window APIs
S5-02.validation: Calendar timezone must be a valid IANA ZoneId. Calendar list paging defaults to page 0/size 20 and caps size at 100; name sorting is allow-listed. Working-day weekday values are 1-7 and closeTime must be later than openTime. Calendar deletion conflicts while windows or calendar-scoped holidays reference it.
S5-02.authorization: Every /api/v1 request, including OPTIONS, forwards the caller bearer token to POST /api/v1/internal/authorization/scheduling. Active users may READ; MANAGE requires current IDENTITY_SYSTEM_ADMIN. Missing credentials, denial, inactive users, and Identity outages fail closed. The actor is derived from the authenticated token; request-supplied actor, role, permission, and scope are not accepted.
S5-02.serviceExposure: All nine operations are served by Scheduling and guarded by the /api/v1/** authorization interceptor. Missing bearer credentials are rejected before controller execution; reads and OPTIONS delegate Identity READ, while mutations and unsupported methods delegate Identity MANAGE. The API Gateway currently has no Scheduling route; Gateway publication is deferred to Stage 11. These are authenticated service routes, not public/Gateway routes. OpenAPI declares bearer authentication for each operation but does not publish the routes. The repository has no deployment ingress policy; production must restrict direct service and OpenAPI access to a private/trusted network.
S5-02.apiContract: Nine operations use Scheduling-owned DTOs, shared ApiResponse/ApiError envelopes, X-Correlation-ID propagation, and per-operation bearer security declarations in OpenAPI.
S5-02.verification: Follow-up PostgreSQL-backed route tests confirm missing credentials are denied, GET delegates READ, POST delegates READ or MANAGE as appropriate, OPTIONS requires authentication and delegates READ, and inactive users are denied by Identity. The complete Scheduling suite passed 50 tests; Identity/common-web passed 44 tests; the full 11-module backend reactor passed 159 tests, with zero failures, errors, or skips.
S5-02.requirementsAndErd: No requirements or ERD change was needed.

S5-03.name: Holiday and closure management APIs
S5-03.scopesAndBehavior: Holidays may be calendar-scoped, building-scoped, scoped to a calendar/building intersection, or nationwide when both IDs are null. Holiday active and blocksBooking state is mutable/filterable; creator attribution is returned by Identity, never supplied by the caller. Closure periods are building-scoped or nationwide with blocksBooking behavior and finite [startsAt, endsAt) ranges stored as PostgreSQL tstzrange.
S5-03.integrity: Flyway V3 adds a NULLS NOT DISTINCT unique index on calendar/building/date to reject duplicate holidays for an exact scope while retaining the ERD's calendar-date unique constraint. Calendar/building references remain scalar IDs except the local working_calendar foreign key.
S5-03.authorization: All /api/v1 operations delegate to Identity: active users may READ; MANAGE requires IDENTITY_SYSTEM_ADMIN. Holiday created_by_user_id comes from the authenticated Identity subject.
S5-03.apiContract: Ten versioned operations use Scheduling DTOs, ApiResponse/ApiError, X-Correlation-ID, and bearer-protected OpenAPI. Scheduling writes no Room maintenance or Booking reservation data.
S5-03.verification: Scheduling PostgreSQL/Testcontainers and API/OpenAPI authorization tests plus the full backend Java test gate passed with no test failures or errors.
S5-03.requirementsAndErd: No requirements or ERD change was needed.

S5-04.name: Recurrence persistence and validation
S5-04.rruleModel: Date-based RRULE supports FREQ=DAILY|WEEKLY|MONTHLY|YEARLY, INTERVAL, BYDAY weekday tokens without ordinal selectors, BYMONTHDAY, BYMONTH, WKST, UNTIL as a strict YYYYMMDD iCalendar DATE, and COUNT. Unknown, repeated, malformed, and unsupported fields are rejected. startsOn must match the rule pattern. At least one of UNTIL or COUNT is required; both may be supplied and constrain evaluation together. The existing ERD ends_on and occurrence_count columns persist the parsed UNTIL and COUNT values.
S5-04.boundsAndEvaluation: COUNT is limited to 365. UNTIL cannot exceed the inclusive horizon startsOn + 1 calendar year. Count-only rules must reach COUNT within that horizon. Rules exceeding either limit are rejected rather than truncated. Evaluation iterates bounded LocalDate values and returns deterministic local occurrence dates together with the IANA timezone; Africa/Kigali is the Rwanda calendar timezone. DST does not shift date-only occurrences. Evaluation does not create booking requests, confirmed reservations, or occupancy; each occurrence requires normal booking/scheduling validation.
S5-04.authorization: All operations delegate to the existing Scheduling Identity authorization policy: active users may READ; MANAGE requires IDENTITY_SYSTEM_ADMIN. created_by_user_id is derived from Identity's authenticated actor, never request data. Missing credentials and Identity failures fail closed.
S5-04.apiContract: Six versioned operations use Scheduling-owned DTOs, bounded list paging, shared ApiResponse/ApiError envelopes, X-Correlation-ID, and bearer-protected OpenAPI.
S5-04.verification: RecurrenceRuleApiTests passed 8 PostgreSQL Testcontainers API tests; the Scheduling suite passed 20 tests; Identity passed 37 tests and common-web 6 tests. The complete 11-module backend reactor passed all 128 tests with zero failures, errors, or skips.
S5-04.requirementsAndErd: No migration, requirements specification, or approved ERD change was required.

S5-05.name: Scheduling constraint validation API
S5-05.requestAndValidation: The versioned read-only validation request contains workingCalendarId, officeBuildingId, startsAt and endsAt Instants, the expected IANA timezone, and an optional persisted recurrenceRuleId. The selected calendar must be active and building-compatible, and its timezone must exactly match the request; a supplied recurrence rule must also use that timezone and start on the submitted local start date. Instants are converted in the selected zone. Intervals must be positive and within one local date; recurrence reuses the submitted local start/end times on each bounded RRULE date. Each interval must fit fully inside a working-day window. Applicable active blocksBooking holidays and overlapping building/nationwide blocking half-open closure ranges invalidate the affected occurrence. The existing S5-04 bound limits evaluation to at most 365 dates.
S5-05.responseAndFailurePolicy: Policy conflicts return HTTP 200 with data.valid=false, checked occurrence count, and occurrence-scoped stable violation codes; consumers must proceed only when valid=true. Malformed intervals, invalid or mismatched timezones, invalid recurrence combinations, missing referenced resources, and Identity authorization/dependency failures return errors rather than approval. Nonexistent recurring wall-clock times during timezone gaps are rejected; ambiguous repeated local times resolve deterministically using the zone's first valid offset.
S5-05.authorization: The validation POST delegates to Identity using READ because it does not mutate state. Identity outages and authorization failures fail closed. Existing mutation endpoints retain their MANAGE authorization policy.
S5-05.apiContract: One versioned POST operation uses Scheduling-owned request/response DTOs, the shared ApiResponse/ApiError envelopes, request correlation, and protected OpenAPI documentation. Scheduling does not call Booking or Room and does not mutate reservations or occupancy.
S5-05.verification: SchedulingConstraintApiTests passed all 8 PostgreSQL Testcontainers API tests. The Scheduling suite passed 28 tests, Identity passed 37 tests, and common-web passed 6 tests. The full 11-module backend reactor passed all 136 tests with zero failures, errors, or skips.
S5-05.requirementsAndErd: No migration, requirements specification, or approved ERD change was required.

S5-06.name: Availability calculation and owner-service integration

request.timeRange: startsAt and endsAt are absolute Instants and define a positive half-open range of no more than 31 days.
request.limits: facilityTypeIds contains at most 25 non-null IDs; candidate output is limited to 5000 windows. Exceeding a limit returns an explicit error and never partial results.

response.semantics: Windows are continuous candidate intervals with explicit Instant boundaries and a local occurrence date. They are not reservation confirmations. For recurrence, each window describes an individual RRULE occurrence; the API does not promise one common interval across the full series.

S5-06.authorization: The public POST route requires a bearer token and delegates read authorization to Identity. The caller's bearer token is forwarded to Room and Booking owner APIs. The internal Booking occupancy endpoint is protected and must not be exposed through the API Gateway.

roomOwnerIntegration.source: Room Service owner APIs only; Scheduling performs no Room database access.
roomOwnerIntegration.policy: Room status, effective room-specific/building rules, WORKING facility assignments, and finite maintenance ranges are checked. Invalid, incomplete, unauthorized, or unavailable authoritative Room responses fail closed.

request.timeRange: Absolute Instants for the requested half-open range.

response.completeness: Every requested room must appear exactly once, even when it has no occupied intervals. Occupied intervals must be finite and half-open.

bookingOccupancyApiContract.intervalOwnership: Booking returns its authoritative occupied intervals inclusive of its configured release buffer; Scheduling does not add a buffer.
bookingOccupancyApiContract.failurePolicy: Missing, unavailable, unauthorized, malformed, incomplete, or stale snapshots fail closed. No missing/failed response may be interpreted as zero occupancy. Until S6 implements the Booking provider, candidate-producing searches return 503 BOOKING_OCCUPANCY_UNAVAILABLE.

bookingOccupancyEventContract.status: Defined for future Booking outbox publication; no event consumer or cached occupancy state is implemented in S5-06.
bookingOccupancyEventContract.occupiedInterval: For UPSERT, the finite half-open interval includes Booking's release buffer. REMOVE identifies the reservation and room with no active occupied interval.
bookingOccupancyEventContract.deliverySemantics: Booking publishes after transaction commit from its outbox. eventId supports deduplication; reservationVersion increases monotonically per reservation so consumers can ignore stale/out-of-order updates. Events are notifications/invalidation only and never replace the synchronous authoritative occupancy snapshot.

S5-06.emptyAndRecurringResults: If no preliminary candidate windows exist, the API may return an empty list without calling Booking and sets bookingOccupancyIncluded=false. Candidate-producing searches require successful occupancy inclusion and otherwise fail closed. Recurring results are occurrence-level only; Booking must validate the full series before confirmation.
S5-06.apiContract: Scheduling-owned validated request/response DTOs, shared ApiResponse/ApiError envelopes, X-Correlation-ID, protected OpenAPI. The API is read-only and writes no Room maintenance or Booking occupancy.
S5-06.verification: Availability calculation covers calendar windows, policy boundaries, maintenance, closures, holidays, working facilities, current occupancy subtraction, recurrence occurrence filtering, timezone/DST handling, dependency failures, and stale/partial occupancy. The S5-06 follow-up focused authorization/API/availability selection passed 23 tests; the complete Scheduling suite passed 50, Identity/common-web passed 44, and the full 11-module backend reactor passed 159 tests, all with zero failures, errors, or skips.
S5-06.requirementsAndErd: No schema migration, SRS, requirements specification, or approved ERD change was required.

schedulingApiExposurePolicy.serverSideEnforcement: Every request, including OPTIONS, requires a bearer token and a successful Identity authorization decision before controller handling.
schedulingApiExposurePolicy.callerIdentity: Authenticated user identity and current active/permission state are resolved by Identity from the forwarded Identity-issued bearer token; Scheduling does not accept caller-supplied actor IDs, roles, permissions, or scope.
schedulingApiExposurePolicy.serviceToService: Authorized upstream services propagate the caller bearer token. No separate machine-to-machine identity credential is implemented in Stage 5.
schedulingApiExposurePolicy.gateway: No Scheduling route is configured on the API Gateway in Stage 5; routing/publication is deferred to Stage 11.
schedulingApiExposurePolicy.networkBoundary: Direct access is available only to callers that can reach the service and pass Identity authorization. The repository contains no production ingress policy; deployment must restrict Scheduling and its OpenAPI surfaces to a private/trusted network.

authorization.userScope: Scoped Admin user listing is filtered to eligible in-building Secretaries and unassigned pending users; single-user operations use the same policy checks.
authorization.organizationPolicy: POST /api/v1/internal/authorization/organization evaluates READ or MANAGE against the authenticated active Identity account and current system-admin permission.
authorization.schedulingPolicy: POST /api/v1/internal/authorization/scheduling allows READ for active Identity accounts and requires IDENTITY_SYSTEM_ADMIN for MANAGE; its actorUserId response supplies trusted Holiday creator attribution.
authorization.roomManagementPolicy: POST /api/v1/internal/authorization/room-management evaluates ROOM_MANAGE for a building scope or global system-admin authority for a null scope, then returns actorUserId from the authenticated principal.
